Nodes and Weights for a Gamma(a, a) Mixing Variable

Source: R/predict_prior.R
gamma_nodes.Rd

A trapezoidal rule in \(v = \log w\) for the \(\mathrm{Gamma}(a, a)\) density, over the range between its quantiles \(10^{-12}\) and \(1 - 10^{-12}\), the weights normalized to sum to one.

Usage

gamma_nodes(a, h = 0.6, k_min = 40L)

Arguments

a

The shape, \(\nu/2\).

h

The spacing of the nodes in \(\log w\).

k_min

The smallest number of nodes.

Value

A list with w, the nodes, and a, the weights, which sum to one.

Details

A prediction's distribution function, averaged over \(w\), depends on \(w\) through \(\sqrt{w/(w + c)}\), which is not smooth at zero, and its tails come from small \(w\). A Gauss-Laguerre rule in \(w\) converges slowly there; in \(\log w\) the integrand decays exponentially at both ends and the trapezoidal rule converges exponentially. Measured on the probability that a Gaussian measurement around a Student t effect falls below the 2.5 per cent quantile, against adaptive quadrature: at \(\nu = 1\) the error is 1e-04 with 40 nodes and 2e-08 with 80, against 1.2e-02 for Gauss-Laguerre with 96; at \(\nu = 2.54\) it is 1e-07 and 4e-13, against 5e-05.

The range widens as \(\nu\) falls (25 units of \(\log w\) at \(\nu = 2.54\), 62 at 0.95, 190 at 0.3), so the rule fixes the spacing of the nodes rather than their number. At a spacing of 0.6 the error is at most 2e-08 from \(\nu = 0.3\) to 2.54, against 7e-05 with 64 nodes at \(\nu = 0.5\); at least 40 nodes are used, which covers a large \(\nu\), where the range is short.

Examples

q <- statmodels7:::gamma_nodes(1.5)
c(length(q$w), sum(q$a), sum(q$a * q$w))
#> [1] 40.000000  1.000000  1.000009
